summary.name: SE Radio Episode 276: Björn Rabenstein on Site Reliability Engineering
summary.one_liner: A Software Engineering Radio podcast interview (with transcript) in which Björn Rabenstein discusses Google-style site reliability engineering (SRE), how it differs from DevOps, and its practices.
use_cases: Learning what SRE means compared with DevOps
Deciding how much reliability a service needs
Structuring monitoring, incident response and postmortems
Balancing on-call work with engineering time
summary.what_it_does: The page is a transcript of a Software Engineering Radio episode with Björn Rabenstein, a production engineer at SoundCloud and Prometheus developer who previously worked as an SRE at Google. Host Robert Blumen and the guest discuss how Google defines SRE as software engineers designing an operational function, and how it differs from DevOps. They cover the 50% rule for operational work, Dickerson's hierarchy of reliability (monitoring at the base, then incident response, postmortems, testing, capacity planning and the product), and the distinction between SLI, SLO and SLA. They also discuss the risk of setting too-high reliability targets, error budgets, and Rabenstein's experience applying SRE ideas at SoundCloud.
notable: Transcript of an SE Radio interview with a former Google SRE and Prometheus developer
Explains Dickerson's hierarchy of reliability, modeled on Maslow's hierarchy
Defines SLI, SLO and SLA and the error budget concept
Links to related SE Radio episodes on DevOps, infrastructure as code and Prometheus monitoring
caveats: Discusses the Google SRE book only in passing; the book itself is not reviewed on this page
Interview is conversational and some passages are unclear or unintelligible in the transcript
